passage: Nursery note, Tuesday. From the doorway I saw Mahima push an arm into the gap behind the sofa, tug at the teddy and fail. Mahima stopped, looked at the gap and walked off to the blocks without a word to anyone. The teddy stayed behind the sofa until I found it much later. At nap time Mahima asked for it and cried when it was not there. I found it and we talked about pointing and saying "stuck." Mehak

qa.q: Where did Mahima walk off to?
qa.a: Mahima walked off to the blocks.

qa.q: What was Mahima feeling at nap time when the teddy was not there?
qa.a: Mahima was sad and missed the teddy, and the crying shows the loss had not been forgotten.

qa.q: What could Mahima try instead of walking away, and why?
qa.a: Mahima could tell Mehak or point at the gap, because an adult can reach the teddy and solve the problem quickly.

qa.q: How does Mehak see the missing teddy?
qa.a: Mehak saw the failed try but was not told, so the teddy was lost until nap time, and Mehak wants Mahima to learn to ask.

grounding: A toddler stops trying to free a wedged teddy, walks away and tells no one, so the toy stays lost until a caregiver finds it later.
